name: Okra Leaf Curl
description: A viral disease causing characteristic upward curling of okra leaves, reduced growth, and poor yield. It is transmitted by whiteflies and is increasingly common in West Africa.
symptoms: Leaf thickening and darkening of veins
Reduced number and quality of pods
Plants may appear bushy with shortened internodes
causes: Okra leaf curl virus transmitted by whiteflies
High whitefly populations in the field
Dry season conditions favoring whitefly reproduction
Infected volunteer okra plants serving as inoculum sources
treatments: No cure once plant is infected
Remove and destroy infected plants early
Apply neem oil or insecticidal soap to control whiteflies
Use reflective mulches to repel whiteflies
prevention: Use whitefly-resistant okra varieties when available
Plant early to avoid peak whitefly populations
Intercrop with tall crops like maize to reduce whitefly landing
Apply botanical insecticides regularly as preventive measure
Maintain field hygiene and remove infected plants promptly
